note: At most ten technically defensible candidates; each requires the stated pending checks before promotion to a hypothesis worker.

candidates.title: Period conjecture for three-parameter Subtraction Nim (Ward/Moriwaki)
candidates.quantifiers: For every S={a,b,c}, 0<a<b<c, c!=a+b: eventual nim period equals one of a+b, b+c, c+a (literal MathDB wording).
candidates.source: MathDB 375237; source arXiv:2606.11658 (Moriwaki 2026) and arXiv:2312.02426; statement read from cached full record only.
candidates.concrete_mechanism: Nim-value recurrence g(n)=mex{g(n-s)}; eventual period of g computed exactly for small S. Literal claim already contradicted: S=(1,3,5) gives g = 1,0,1,0,... eventual period 2, and 2 notin {4,8,6}. 37 further witnesses in a<6,b<11,c<15 (screening/witness-375237.json).
candidates.first_decisive_calculation: DONE (bounded): mex table to n=600, minimal full-tail period on g[300:600]. Primary witness S=(1,3,5): period 2.
candidates.certificate_size: Tiny: nim table for n<=41 plus period check; a Lean/witness certificate is a few dozen integers.
candidates.required_infrastructure: None (integer arithmetic). Primary-source read of 2606.11658/2312.02426 to fix literal wording is the only dependency.
candidates.strongest_obstruction: Wording risk: if the source asserts the period divides one of a+b,b+c,c+a (or defines period with preperiod), the refutation fails; then the claim becomes a divisibility statement needing its own analysis.
candidates.bounded_attempt_scope: 1-2 sessions: read source wording; if 'equals', write counterexample note with witness table; if 'divides', test the divisibility form on the same witness set.
candidates.prior_risk: Ward's conjecture literature; the two index papers may already discuss the period-2 phenomenon (their theorems may exclude it via hypotheses).

candidates.title: Period-equality of nim-sequences and zero-position sequences (Ho)
candidates.quantifiers: For every subtraction game S: eventual period of G(n) equals eventual period of V(n)=1_{G(n)!=0}.
candidates.concrete_mechanism: V is a function of G within one period, so per(V) divides per(G); equality fails only if the zero-pattern inside a nim period is invariant under a nontrivial shift. Search for such a symmetry; for |S|<=2 use explicit period structure.
candidates.first_decisive_calculation: DONE (bounded): exhaustive mex computation, no violation for 1-element (a<=14), 2-element (a<10,b<15), 3-element (a<6,b<11,c<15) sets, tail 300 periods on 600 samples.
candidates.certificate_size: Counterexample: one period block. Proof: explicit period formulas for |S|<=2 plus structure lemma; moderate.
candidates.required_infrastructure: Integer arithmetic only; optionally Sage for period enumeration.
candidates.strongest_obstruction: For general S the nim period is not explicitly known; equality of minimal periods needs a structural argument about zero positions that may not exist (a large-S counterexample is plausible).
candidates.bounded_attempt_scope: 1-2 sessions: extend search to 4-element sets and larger periods; attempt |S|=2 proof; abandon if counterexample search exceeds ~10^8 states without hit and no structure emerges.
candidates.prior_risk: Ho's paper and successors may contain the 2-element case or a known counterexample; subtraction-games literature is active.

candidates.title: GCD of coefficients of c_m(c_1) is a power of two (Kitaev-Vartanian, Painleve III)
candidates.quantifiers: For every m>=2, gcd of coefficients of the polynomial c_m(c_1) equals 2^{z_m} for some integer z_m>=1.
candidates.concrete_mechanism: Exact rational recurrence for c_m polynomials; track coefficient gcd under the recurrence; prove the gcd evolution stays a power of two by 2-adic valuation bookkeeping.
candidates.first_decisive_calculation: PENDING: extract recurrence from source; compute gcd(c_m) for m<=50; if a non-power-of-2 appears, bounded counterexample; else extract z_m pattern and attempt induction.
candidates.certificate_size: Small: recurrence + gcd table + induction; formalizable as integer computation.
candidates.required_infrastructure: Python fractions/sympy; bounded read of the recurrence section of 2305.17278.
candidates.strongest_obstruction: The recurrence may couple c_m to earlier c_j with odd factors that are hard to control; z_m pattern may be irregular beyond computed range.
candidates.bounded_attempt_scope: 1-2 sessions: extraction + computation + pattern attempt; stop if no clean 2-adic pattern by m=50.
candidates.prior_risk: Painleve-coefficient arithmetic may have been studied in follow-ups; cite-check 2305.17278 citing papers.

candidates.title: Eigenvalue multiplicities and semisimplicity for Stern recurrence matrices (Stanley)
candidates.quantifiers: For all s>=1: e_{2s-1}(0)=s/3+[0,-1/3,1/3]_3; 0 semisimple, no other multiple eigenvalues, 1 not an eigenvalue; e_{2s}(1), e_{2s}(-1) as given; 1 and -1 semisimple, no other multiples.
candidates.concrete_mechanism: A_r matrices have small block/affine structure; derive recurrence for characteristic polynomials, factor over Z, compare multiplicities; semisimplicity via rank(A_r-theta I) computations.
candidates.first_decisive_calculation: PENDING: build A_r for r<=12 from 1901.04647 definitions, compute characteristic polynomials exactly, verify the four displayed formulas numerically-symbolically.
candidates.certificate_size: Moderate: symbolic recurrence + factorization identities; formalizable.
candidates.required_infrastructure: sympy/Python ints; bounded read of Stanley's definitions.
candidates.strongest_obstruction: A_r dimension grows with r; need genuine recurrence for char polys, not direct eigencomputation at large r.
candidates.prior_risk: Stern diatomic array literature is active (1990s-2020s); Stanley's paper is the canonical reference and its open problems may have been picked up.

candidates.title: Sills-Zeilberger structural conjecture for P_{01r}(N)
candidates.quantifiers: For every r>=1: P_{01r}(N)=(-1)^N N! (-4)^r r! C_{01(N-r)}(N) is monic, alternating, convex, degree 2r, with only real roots 0 and 1.
candidates.concrete_mechanism: Explicit coefficient formulas for C_{01r} from partial fractions; prove root/convexity structure by induction on r using the recursion recorded in the source.
candidates.first_decisive_calculation: PENDING: compute P_{01r} for r<=8 exactly; verify all four properties; identify the induction step.
candidates.strongest_obstruction: 'Only real roots 0 and 1' is a strong global statement; induction may give degree/convexity but not root location without a sign-explicit coefficient formula.
candidates.bounded_attempt_scope: 1-2 sessions; stop if roots drift from {0,1} at moderate r (would indicate misread statement).
candidates.prior_risk: O'Sullivan's paper and Sills-Zeilberger's original A005704-type work; check citing literature for partial results.

candidates.title: Louboutin polynomial identity for S_{a,b} (and R_{a,b})
candidates.quantifiers: For all nonzero integers a,b (c=a+b!=0) and d in {a,b,c}: P_{|d|}(S_{a,b}(T),S_{a,b}(1/T)) = -S_{a,b}(1/T^{|d|}); plus the even/odd-a companion identity for R_{a,b}.
candidates.concrete_mechanism: Expand P_d by its binomial-sum definition; the identity is coefficientwise; proof by regenerating the binomial convolution identities; machine-verifiable.
candidates.first_decisive_calculation: PENDING but cheap: verify identity symbolically for d<=30 and random a,b. MANDATORY first: read 2410.21158 to check whether the paper proves this lemma en route (statement says the identity is 'used in the proof').
candidates.strongest_obstruction: If the paper proves it, no credit (routine lemma); if unproved, the binomial-sum manipulation may still need care for the R-case signs.
candidates.bounded_attempt_scope: Half session for the source check; one session for a proof if genuinely open.
candidates.prior_risk: HIGH that it is already proved inside 2410.21158; Louboutin's original note may also contain it.

candidates.title: Marques-Trojovsky explicit Bonse threshold values Psi(x)
candidates.concrete_mechanism: Exact finite verification on sieves plus analytic tail bounds (primorial vs prime powers) to close each interval; existence of Psi needs a global convergence argument from the source.
candidates.first_decisive_calculation: PARTIALLY DONE (bounded): no violations for n in [21,6000) at x=0.9,1.3; none in [149,6000) at x=0.5,0.8; max failing n=1096 in window for x=0.3,0.4. Claims (iii)-(v) require sieves to n~6e7 and tail estimates.
candidates.certificate_size: Computational: primorial log table + verification script + tail-bound lemma; moderate.
candidates.required_infrastructure: Sieves (pure Python OK, 8e7 primes within caps in chunks); careful k(n,x) monotonicity in x.
candidates.strongest_obstruction: Tail: k(n,x)-pi(pi(n)) growth vs log-primorial growth needs explicit analytic estimates, not just computation, for 'for all n>=m'.
candidates.bounded_attempt_scope: 2 sessions; verify (i)-(ii) fully, (iii) computationally; (iv)-(v) only if infrastructure permits chunked sieves.
candidates.prior_risk: Root may classify as routine parameter computation; the source may already prove (i)-(ii) partially. Read 2511.13691 body first.

candidates.title: Unimodality of the two-variable Shi distance enumerator
candidates.quantifiers: For fixed n,k, the sequence Dist_n(k,l) over l is unimodal.
candidates.concrete_mechanism: Two-variable distance enumerator of the Shi arrangement has known product/combinatorial formulas; obtain explicit Dist_n(k,l) and prove unimodality in l (e.g., real-rootedness of the l-polynomial or an injection).
candidates.first_decisive_calculation: PENDING: compute Dist_n(k,l) for n<=8 from the source formula; test unimodality; identify the closed form.
candidates.certificate_size: Small-moderate if a product form exists.
candidates.strongest_obstruction: If no closed formula for the bivariate enumerator exists, the problem reverts to raw arrangement counting.
candidates.prior_risk: 2006 open problem may have been handled in Shi arrangement literature; cite-check.

candidates.title: Finiteness of odd n with s(n)=s(n^2)=14 or 15
candidates.quantifiers: For k in {14,15}: finitely many odd n with s_2(n)=s_2(n^2)=k.
candidates.source: MathDB 381656; source arXiv:2203.05451 (proves k in {9,10,11} case analysis).
candidates.concrete_mechanism: Extend the source's finite-case method: n^2 with digit sum k has n^2 = sum of k powers of 2; structural constraints (n odd => n^2=1 mod 8) plus exhaustive search/elimination.
candidates.first_decisive_calculation: PENDING: read the 9-11 proof mechanism; replicate the search structure for 14,15 beyond 2^80.
candidates.certificate_size: Computational plus case elimination; potentially large but bounded.
candidates.required_infrastructure: Chunked search code within caps; bounded read of 2203.05451.
candidates.strongest_obstruction: The 9-11 method may not scale to 14,15 (case explosion); finiteness proofs for digit-sum constraints are generically hard.
candidates.bounded_attempt_scope: 2 sessions; abandon if the source mechanism does not transfer.
candidates.prior_risk: Stolarsky-type bounds on s(n^2) and later work (2022-2026) may already treat larger k.

candidates.title: Xin's second determinant factorization conjecture
candidates.quantifiers: For odd n: det_{0<=i,j<=n-1}(-delta_{ij}+binom(mu+i+j, j+2)) equals the explicit product in Krattenthaler math/0503507 (to be read from source).
candidates.source: MathDB 378937; source arXiv:math/0503507 (Krattenthaler 2005), where the first conjecture of the family is resolved and this one is stated open for odd n.
candidates.concrete_mechanism: Determinant evaluation: condensation/Dodgson, row-column operations, or recognition as a known orthogonal-polynomial/Wronskian determinant; odd/even asymmetry suggests a pairing argument.
candidates.first_decisive_calculation: PENDING: verify numerically for n=3,5,7,9 and fit the product; then attempt symbolic proof. Cache statement is mangled (cdet artifacts); literal statement must be re-read from the source PDF.
candidates.strongest_obstruction: Even-n failure means the odd case uses a genuine structural feature; if no mechanism is visible, it may be genuinely hard.
candidates.prior_risk: Determinant-evaluation conjectures from Krattenthaler's complement have been worked on; check citing literature.
